item.title: How a bank collapse left millions in limbo and toppled Paraguay's president
item.description: A bank's collapse in Paraguay left millions locked out of their money, toppled the president and exposed a web of political and financial ties.

item.title: The world's largest telecoms firm is on trial and the outcome has global implications
item.description: Huawei, the world's biggest telecommunications company, is on trial in New York, accused of stealing American technology and evading US sanctions.

item.title: Trying to find true owners, Paris' Musee D'Orsay exhibits art looted by Nazis
item.description: A new permanent exhibition at Paris' Musee d'Orsay showcases works of art suspected to have been looted by Nazis during the Second World War in France. Experts are trying to find the true owners or their descendants.

item.title: Europe to join U.S.-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, defying Kremlin objections
item.description: France says European officials will attend this week's U.S.-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, the first three-way round of negotiations since February.

item.title: No clear winner in New Zealand election, as leaders prepare for weeks of talks

item.title: A desert stirs to life: Chile's Atacama erupts in its biggest floral display in decades
item.description: El Niño rains have transformed Chile's Atacama Desert into a spectacular sea of color, awakening a fleeting ecosystem of flowers and wildlife in one of the driest places on Earth.
